key_insight: Mechanistic interpretability can fail at the objective level: a faithfulness metric may prefer a circuit that is less behaviorally accurate even when the better mechanism is equally sized.
engineering_relevance: For automated circuit discovery, improving search or attribution is not enough unless the evaluation objective reliably ranks truly better circuits above worse ones.
method: Compare validation faithfulness against held-out behavioral agreement under ordinary resampling.
Test controlled reference edits plus outputs from EAP, EAP-IG, ACDC, and Edge-SP.
Diagnose context distortion by restoring excluded signals from intact-model execution.
evidence_signal: Across four human-reference tasks and InterpBench, KL under resampling misranked 9.4%–41.2% of candidate pairs, and restoring signals fixed 96 of 100 persistent misrankings.
watch_item: The behavioral criterion depends on held-out prompt agreement (or semantic accuracy on Greater-Than), so conclusions may shift with different task definitions or resampling choices.
paper_title: Are We Recovering Mechanisms? Objective-Level Recovery Gaps in Mechanistic Interpretability
